subject: Compiler-aligned WVB 1.36 write-region lifetime containment
claim: The Windows source-built compiler-aligned verifier accepts exact WVB 1.36 write-region candidates, rejects bounded structural, canonical-layout, lifetime-escape, scratch-reuse, and payload-extraction cases, retains the inherited WVB 1.33/1.35 unsafe-scratch matrix, and leaves execution closed.

runs.target: WVB 1.36 write-region source, WVIR, byte contract, containment, and closed execution boundary
Inherited WVB 1.33 construction and WVB 1.35 immutable scratch observation

limitations: The focused write-region oracle covered 13 source cases, seven malformed WVIR mutations, five malformed WVB mutations, four semantic WVB forgeries, and 13 compiler-verifier decisions; it was not the complete changed-file development plan.

The source analyzer can still represent the two unsafe escape and scratch-reuse candidates; the compiler-aligned WVB verifier is the current admission boundary that rejects them, and an earlier source diagnostic remains future usability work.
The verifier conservatively keeps the scratch unavailable through function exit and forbids region payload extraction, so this checkpoint does not execute success or failure behavior.

WVB synthesized type names do not preserve source generic arguments; the verifier proves exact layouts and consistency of the explicit scratch, region, and ABI relation rather than reconstructing erased generic metadata.
The scalar provider, native lowerer, pointer derivation, authenticated Foreign-call path, migrated runtime or OS boundary, and operating-system consumers do not admit WVB 1.36.
The run is local Windows development evidence and does not claim Linux reproduction, paired-host conformance, qualification, release, or independent reproduction.
